hook.line: Everybody's learning RAG, agents and model training, but top-paying AI roles pay you to evaluate, not create.
hook.visual: Close-up of the creator holding a fuzzy lav mic to the lens; from 1.1 s a diagram (RAG, multi-agent, model training) pops in above his head for each skill he names.

beats.what: Close selfie framing, mic held up to camera, bold italic caption 'EVERYBODY'S LEARNING RAG'
A new diagram image flashes in at the top for each skill named: RAG architecture, multi-agent workflow, model training
Pixel-font 'Claude Code' logo card above his head as he turns: roles pay you to evaluate, not create
Dark text screenshot 'Key Insight: RAG + Agents = 70%+ of use cases' backs up the claim
Highlighted article quote about how many companies already run agents and RAG
Screenshot of an expert's post on why AI software is less predictable than normal software
'How AI Hallucination Happens' diagram while he says LLM output is unpredictable
'AI Engineer Salaries' bar chart on '500K plus'
Real job description with evaluation duties highlighted in blue, face shrinks to a small box at the bottom
Screenshots of his community: member list, then course modules, as he lists what it includes

why_it_works: 'Everyone does X, but the money is in Y' contrast sets up a gap the viewer wants closed in the first 8 s
Every claim is followed within a second by a screenshot, chart or job post, so the argument feels sourced rather than opinion
Visuals change about every 2 s (median shot 1.93 s) while the face stays in the same spot, so the eye has new proof to read without losing the speaker
The mic held up to the lens makes the selfie framing feel like a direct, intimate tip
weaknesses: The last 15 s are a community pitch; the evaluation advice itself is never explained
Many screenshots are dense paragraphs too small to read on a phone
The CTA word is cut off at the end of the audio, so the keyword is only in the caption text
for_robert: Pop a proof image (chart, post, job ad) above his head the instant he makes each claim; Fred could carry or unroll each one in from the side instead of it just appearing.
